title: Septinsular Republic
capsule: The Septinsular Republic (Επτάνησος Πολιτεία) was established by the Treaty of Constantinople (1800) following a joint Russo-Ottoman expulsion of French Revolutionary forces from the Ionian Islands — the first autonomous Greek-administered state since the Byzantine era. Governed by a noble oligarchy through an Ionian Senate at Corfu, it passed through three constitutions (1800, 1803, 1806), the last effectively granting Russia intervention rights. The Treaty of Tilsit (July 1807) transferred the islands to Napoleonic France; British forces conquered them piecemeal between 1809 and 1814, reconstituting them as the United States of the Ionian Islands under British protection, which eventually united with Greece in 1864.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The seven islands comprising the republic are precisely identified; their internal administrative boundaries are well documented from Venetian, Ottoman, and Russian archival sources.
